findings.status: clarification recommended; existing counts are correct
findings.location: sections/claim_protocol.tex:27; artifact README Inputs and outputs; sections/audit_appendix.tex:14
findings.exact_text: The portable artifact contains the fixed 126-case manifest, original action streams, per-event reference digests, settings, an unchanged engine and board copy, pinned dependencies, witnesses and negative certificates.
evidence: The 126 records contain 60 elimination cases and 66 default cases. The default cases contain 132 attempts and multiple diagnostics, not one homogeneous certificate each.

There are 70 well-formed target attempts: 63 reachable and seven above cash. One target is malformed and 61 attempts have no parseable target. At decision level, 63 of 66 contain a reachable target; all 66 have some construction witness.
Independent source checks matched all 126 cases and 132 attempt records. The paper largely preserves these units, but the count is easy to compress into an inflated 126-certificates claim.
findings.limit: This is not an accusation that the manuscript currently claims 126 independent trials. It does not. The suggested clarification protects the method's stated contribution.
findings.replacement: The 126 entries are case records, not homogeneous proofs: sixty elimination prefixes and sixty-six default decisions. Attempt-level diagnostics and decision-level existence claims are reported separately; malformed or absent targets receive no impossibility certificate.
findings.bounded_fix: Add this sentence near the first 126-case description, or include the claim-unit table supplied in review.md.

findings.exact_text: The accompanying portable certificate bundle reproduces the 126-case census without access to the repository checkout after dependency installation.
evidence: run_audit.py:291 and 317 consume cases.json; check_default consumes its copied attempts. The portable inputs do not include complete original decisions.jsonl records.

findings.exact_text: Nine adversarial tests reject altered inputs and invalid certificates.
evidence: All nine supplied tests pass in the reviewed package.

The tests include positive witness execution, target-multiset comparison, a guarded search regression, and rejected engine actions. They are not nine independent attempts to pass invalid serialized certificates to a standalone proof checker.
The runner constructs results by live engine execution; it does not expose a general API to validate arbitrary externally supplied certificate objects.
findings.replacement: Nine regression tests exercise input integrity, witness legality, purchase preservation, payment completion and refusal to certify an unsupported sale graph.
findings.bounded_fix: Replace the sentence. Optionally add that the runner constructs and executes the retained proofs rather than acting as a general external certificate checker.

resolved_or_not_reasserted: Generic atomic-sale graph completeness is not claimed by the current guarded implementation; its sole historical negative graph remains valid under the documented mortgage-only restriction.
The 573 ENDs with no detected conflict are not described as verified voluntary holds in the current manuscript.
The 43/63 and 34/42 development rates have explicit, distinct denominators and are not used as independent-trial or model-capability estimates.
The current title, abstract and conclusion do not promise a model ranking, general deception rate, causal persuasion estimate, or capability-alignment trend.
The current related work no longer relies on older broad claims that competitors lack all retries, failure accounting or counterfactual rerunning. I did not independently re-browse those sources.
